prompt.context_jp: 十年前の家族旅行の記憶が、圭介の胸の奥から静かに立ち上がっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 十年前の家族旅行の記憶___、圭介の胸の奥から静かに立ち上がっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best introduces this new scene element.

feedback.correct_en: The memory is being newly introduced as something that spontaneously rose up — new information, so が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the memory as an already-established topic, which doesn't match the sudden onset here. を is wrong because 立ち上がる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: その記憶は今も鮮明だ。
contrast_examples.en: That memory (as topic) is still vivid.

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵が旅行の思い出を話している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最後に行った家族旅行___ 水族館で あなたが携帯電話をなくしたうえに…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up 'the last family trip' as the topic she's describing?

feedback.correct_en: She's taking 'the last family trip' as the topic she's about to tell a story about — classic は usage.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as newly-introduced info in a focus structure, which doesn't fit her reminiscing. に would wrongly treat it as a destination.

contrast_examples.jp: あの旅行は楽しかった。
あの旅行が最高だった。

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵が圭介を責めている。
prompt.prompt_jp: もう お昼じゃない あなた___ 道 間違えるから
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'you' as the one specifically to blame?

feedback.correct_en: She's pinpointing him as THE cause ('it's because YOU got the directions wrong'). This exhaustive/identifying nuance takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたは would sound like a general topic statement, not an accusation singling him out. も ('also') doesn't fit the blame context.

contrast_examples.en: YOU are the one at fault.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が麻衣にベルーガを見せている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気に入った？ ベルーガ お父さん___好きなんだ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle expresses 'Dad TOO likes them (just like you might)'?

feedback.correct_en: He's adding himself to the group that likes belugas — 'me too' calls for も.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like a contrast ('as for Dad...') and が would newly identify who likes them, missing the inclusive feel.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は好き（けど彼は嫌い）。

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が電話に出ない。貴恵がイライラしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハァ… 出ない どこ行ったのよ？ あの人___
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits her frustrated 'as for THAT guy...' tone?

feedback.correct_en: She's singling out 'that guy' with a contrastive/topic は — tossing him out as the subject of her exasperation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would freshly identify who went where, but she already knows who she's complaining about. を doesn't fit intransitive 行く.

contrast_examples.en: Where is that guy (talking about him)?

prompt.context_jp: シャチショーに間に合わなかったことを責めている。
prompt.prompt_jp: シャチショー 終わっちゃった___ないの
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'the orca show (of all things) ended!'?

feedback.correct_en: じゃないの is the set emphatic ending here — 'The orca show ENDED, didn't it!'
feedback.incorrect_en: は or を don't form the exclamatory 〜じゃないの pattern that expresses her reproach.

contrast_examples.jp: 終わっちゃったじゃないの。

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が麻衣を叱っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: あの金___ ご飯代として渡してんの
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up 'that money' as the topic of her lecture?

feedback.correct_en: She's taking 'that money' as the known topic and commenting on its purpose — は is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly-identified info, but the money is already shared knowledge between them.

contrast_examples.en: This money is (as topic) for food.

prompt.context_jp: 求人票を見ながら圭介が娘を励ます。
prompt.prompt_jp: 麻衣 パソコン___得意だし いいんじゃないか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'you're good AT computers' (property of Mai)?

feedback.correct_en: With adjectives like 得意 (be good at), the thing you're good at is marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: を can't mark the object of a stative adjective. は would work in a strong contrastive reading but is less natural here as a plain compliment.

contrast_examples.jp: 英語は得意だ（が数学は苦手）。
contrast_examples.en: I'm good at English (but bad at math) — contrast.

prompt.context_jp: 友利が圭介を観察して言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: こないだは やたら 機嫌___ よかったと思ったら…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'your MOOD was really good' (describing a property)?

feedback.correct_en: 機嫌がいい is a fixed collocation — 'mood is good' always takes が on 機嫌.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would force an awkward contrast; に has no grammatical fit here.

prompt.context_jp: 先輩が客に麻衣を紹介する。
prompt.prompt_jp: こちらの新島___ 担当させていただきます
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Niijima as the (newly identified) person in charge?

feedback.correct_en: Introducing someone new to the client — 'This one, Niijima, will be handling it' — uses が to identify the agent.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat Niijima as already-known topic; the client is just now being introduced to her.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be the one in charge (identifying).

prompt.context_jp: 社長が息子に言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: お前___ やんなくて どうすんだよ？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle emphasizes 'if YOU (of all people) don't do it...'?

feedback.correct_en: Exhaustive-listing が: 'If YOU (specifically) don't do it, who will?' pinpoints the son as the only candidate.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like a mild topic shift and lose the pointed emphasis the father needs.

contrast_examples.en: As for you, aren't you going to?

prompt.context_jp: 守屋が自分の弁当について控えめに言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 卵焼き___ ちょっと自信あるんです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits 'the rolled egg (at least / in contrast) I'm a bit confident about'?

feedback.correct_en: だけは carries the modest 'at least this one thing' nuance she wants — the rolled egg among her lunch items is the one she's proud of.
feedback.incorrect_en: Plain が would just identify the subject without the self-deprecating 'only this' flavor. も would mean 'also,' implying she's confident about other things too.

contrast_examples.jp: 卵焼きだけは自信ある。
contrast_examples.en: At least the rolled egg, I'm confident in.
I'm confident in the rolled egg too.

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵からのLINEに既読がついた瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 既読___ つきました！
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the sudden announcement 'the read-receipt appeared!'?

feedback.correct_en: A brand-new event just happened — 'read-receipt appeared!' This spontaneous occurrence takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it sound like a general statement about 既読. を doesn't fit intransitive つく.

contrast_examples.en: As for a reply, it doesn't come.

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵が自分の忙しさを強調する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ って いろいろあるんだから
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits 'I TOO have things going on' (contrasting her life with his assumptions)?

feedback.correct_en: 私だって is the set emphatic phrase 'even I / I too have...' — pushing back against being treated as always available.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は alone misses the 'even I' emphasis. を is grammatically unfit here.

prompt.context_jp: 蓮司が麻衣のマニュアルを見て感心する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 付箋いっぱい… すげえ細かい字で書き込んであって ___ んだなって
prompt.prompt_en: Which best fills in 'you've been working hard, huh'?

feedback.correct_en: Seeing all those detailed notes, he recognizes her effort — 頑張ってる (working hard) fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: 驚いてる (surprised) and 困ってる (troubled) describe wrong emotional states; her notes signal effort, not confusion.

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が友利を叱る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鍵くらい ___ って言ってんでしょ
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb goes with 鍵 (lock)?

feedback.correct_en: 鍵をかける is the fixed collocation for 'lock the door.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 鍵をつける means to attach a lock; 開ける means to open — the opposite of what she wants.

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が友利を批判する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分のことを___ 口先だけは立派なんだから
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'ignoring your own faults'?

feedback.correct_en: 棚に上げる literally 'put up on a shelf' = ignore/set aside one's own issues while criticizing others.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手に取る means 'pick up,' and 目に入れて doesn't form the right idiom here.

contrast_examples.jp: 自分のことは棚に上げる。

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が万理華を誘う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 旅行に___か？
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best fits inviting her on a trip?

feedback.correct_en: 旅行に行く is the standard phrase; the negative-question form 行かないか is a soft invitation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見ない/来ない don't form natural invitations to a trip from the speaker's side.

contrast_examples.en: Want to go on a trip?

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が自分の家族について話す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 父親___ いないの
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'as for a father, (I) don't have one'?

feedback.correct_en: With negative existence statements that single out a topic ('as for X, there isn't one'), は is natural — she's commenting on the father slot as topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 父親がいない is also grammatical but presents it as fresh info; here は matches her softer, revealing tone about her family. を doesn't fit いる.

contrast_examples.en: As for a father, (I) don't have one.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が仕事の話をする。
prompt.prompt_jp: お客さん___ 頑張ってるねって言ってもらえた
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the customer as the one who said it to her?

feedback.correct_en: With 〜てもらう, the giver/source of the action is marked with に — 'had the customer tell me...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the customer as the simple subject, but with もらう structure the source takes に. で marks means/location.

contrast_examples.en: I was praised by the teacher.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生に教えてもらった。
contrast_examples.en: I had the teacher teach me.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が水族館で貴恵を探す。
prompt.prompt_jp: すいません ___ なんですけど この子 見ませんでしたか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'lost child/person'?

feedback.correct_en: 迷子 means 'lost child' — exactly what he's asking about.
feedback.incorrect_en: 迷惑 means 'trouble/bother'; 遠慮 means 'reserve/restraint.' Neither fits a missing-person inquiry.

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が無事に戻り、二人を軽く叱る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大体 ___ のよ 2人とも
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits 'you two are being overdramatic'?

feedback.correct_en: 大げさ = 'exaggerated/overdramatic' — fits her teasing dismissal of their panic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大変 means 'tough/awful' and 大丈夫 means 'okay' — neither captures 'you're overreacting.'

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が圭介をたしなめる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 話を ___ 進めないでくれる？
prompt.prompt_en: Which fills in 'don't go ahead on your own'?

feedback.correct_en: 勝手に = 'on one's own/arbitrarily,' matching her complaint that he's jumping ahead without her input.
feedback.incorrect_en: 丁寧に ('politely') and 静かに ('quietly') don't match her annoyance at his unilateral planning.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介がメッセージを送りすぎた理由を説明する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'I couldn't reach you, so I got worried'?

choices.text: 連絡も取れなかったから なんか心配になっちゃって
連絡も取れなかったから なんか心配をしちゃって

feedback.correct_en: 心配になる expresses the natural shift INTO a worried state; it matches his gradually mounting anxiety.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配をする exists but sounds like a deliberate action ('to worry about'); it clashes with the spontaneous なんか ('somehow') tone here.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が張り切って予定を立てた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'My prep was perfect'?

choices.text: 予習は完璧って言っただろ？
予習は満点って言っただろ？

feedback.correct_en: 完璧 ('perfect/flawless') naturally collocates with 予習 for preparation. It also echoes his line from ten years ago.
feedback.incorrect_en: 満点 is used for test scores, not for describing preparation quality — it would sound off here.

contrast_examples.en: I got a perfect score on the test.

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵を見つけた圭介のセリフ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for his relieved reaction?

choices.text: よかった～ もう一生 会えないかと…
よかった～ もう一生 会わないかと…

feedback.correct_en: 会えない (potential negative, 'can't meet') fits the fear of losing her forever — out of his control.
feedback.incorrect_en: 会わない is simple negative ('won't meet'), implying a volitional refusal, which doesn't match his panic.

contrast_examples.jp: もう会えないかと思った。
contrast_examples.en: I thought I'd never be able to see you again.
I don't intend to meet again.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が初仕事への不安を話す。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'I'm nervous'?

choices.text: お客さんの所 行くんだけど 緊張する
お客さんの所 行くんだけど 緊張される

feedback.correct_en: 緊張する ('I feel nervous') is the standard self-description of one's own emotional state.
feedback.incorrect_en: 緊張される would mean someone else is tense toward you (passive/honorific) — doesn't fit expressing one's own nerves.

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が友利を叱咤する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for criticizing someone's pride?

choices.text: ハート弱いくせに プライドだけは 一丁前
ハート弱いくせに プライドだけは 一丁前だ強い

feedback.correct_en: 一丁前 alone functions as the predicate ('full-grown/grown-up-level'); adding 強い is redundant and ungrammatical.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B piles 一丁前だ強い together, which doesn't form a natural phrase in Japanese.

contrast_examples.en: At least your mouth is grown-up level.

prompt.context_jp: 万理華が麻衣を問い詰める。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今日___ 家にいるって 言ってたわよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets today as the contrastive topic in the accusation?

feedback.correct_en: は highlights 'today' as the specific day under discussion, implicitly contrasting with other days — exactly her pointed tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly identify which day, but the day is already shared context. に alone marks time but misses the topical/contrastive force.

contrast_examples.jp: 今日に限って出かけた。
contrast_examples.en: Of all days, today she went out.

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵がベルーガの寿命を疑問に思う。
prompt.prompt_jp: ベルーガ___ そんなに長生き？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle takes 'belugas' as the topic of her question?

feedback.correct_en: って here is the colloquial topic marker (= は), suitable for raising 'belugas' as the thing she's wondering about.
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't fit the stative 長生き predicate, and に has no role as topic marker here.

contrast_examples.jp: ベルーガってかわいい。
